Numbered badges give the topological order, in which every node comes after all nodes with arrows into it. The result card lists A, B, D, C, E, F." width="100%"} Returns a linear ordering of nodes such that for every directed edge `u -> v`, node `u` appears before `v` in the ordering. This is only possible for directed acyclic graphs (DAGs). Uses Kahn's algorithm (BFS-based) which has `O(V + E)` time complexity. The algorithm processes nodes with zero in-degree first, then removes them and updates in-degrees of neighbors. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : node IDs in topological order. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is undirected or contains a cycle (not a DAG). ::: ## Common Use Cases {.doc-common-use-cases} - build systems and dependency resolution - task scheduling with prerequisites - package installation order - Makefile execution order - database migration ordering - course curriculum planning ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Kahn's algorithm (1962) drives the sort: it maintains an in-degree count for every node, seeds a queue with the zero-in-degree nodes (the ones nothing else depends on), repeatedly dequeues, and decrements the in-degrees of each dequeued node's successors. Cycle detection falls out for free: if the queue empties before every node has been visited, at least one node must sit inside a cycle, and the implementation raises `ValueError` rather than silently returning a truncated result. Time and space are both $O(V + E)$. The output ordering is not unique in general; any node whose entire ancestor set has already appeared is eligible next, and the arbitrary tie-break here is whichever one the underlying queue serves first. ## Examples {.doc-examples} A small build dependency graph sorts so that every file appears after the files it depends on: ::: {#53a76e14 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["main.cpp", "utils.cpp", "utils.h", "config.h"]) .add_edges( [ ("main.cpp", "utils.h"), # main depends on utils.h ("main.cpp", "config.h"), # main depends on config.h ("utils.cpp", "utils.h"), # utils.cpp depends on utils.h ("utils.h", "config.h"), # utils.h depends on config.h ] ) ) order_ids = graph.topological_sort() # config.h and utils.h always precede the files that depend on them [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in order_ids] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['main.cpp', 'utils.cpp', 'utils.h', 'config.h'] ``` ::: ::: The same idea applies to course prerequisites, where the ordering doubles as a valid semester-by-semester curriculum: ::: {#f1984565 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["Intro CS", "Data Structures", "Algorithms", "Machine Learning"]) .add_edges( [ ("Intro CS", "Data Structures"), ("Data Structures", "Algorithms"), ("Algorithms", "Machine Learning"), ] ) ) curriculum_ids = graph.topological_sort() # Returns courses in an order that always satisfies prerequisites [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in curriculum_ids] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` ['Intro CS', 'Data Structures', 'Algorithms', 'Machine Learning'] ``` ::: ::: A circular dependency has no valid ordering, so a cyclic graph raises an error instead of silently returning a partial result: ::: {#9f45a0b0 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges( [ ("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "A"), # Creates a cycle ] ) ) error_message = None try: graph.topological_sort() except ValueError as e: # The graph is cyclic, so no valid ordering exists error_message = str(e) error_message ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` 'Graph contains a cycle - not a DAG. Processed 0 of 3 nodes' ``` ::: ::: When a graph has multiple valid orderings, any one of them may be returned: ::: {#567effb4 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C"]) .add_edges([("A", "C"), ("B", "C")]) ) # Both [A, B, C] and [B, A, C] are valid; C always comes last order = graph.topological_sort() [graph.get_label_from_id(nid) for nid in order] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` ['B', 'A', 'C'] ``` ::: :::
